chunks.source: PM-Kisan Portal - Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
chunks.content:
Overview:
PM-KISAN is a Central Sector Scheme that provides income support to all landholding farmers' families in the country to enable them to take care of expenses related to agriculture and allied activities as well as domestic needs.

chunks.source: PM-Kisan Portal - Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
chunks.content:
Benefits:
- Under the scheme, financial benefit of Rs. 6,000/- per year is provided to all landholding farmer families.
- The benefit is transferred in three equal installments of Rs. 2,000/- each, every four months.
- The amount is transferred directly to the bank accounts of the beneficiaries through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode.

chunks.source: PM-Kisan Portal - Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
chunks.content:
Eligibility Criteria:
- All landholding farmers' families who have cultivable landholding in their names are eligible.
- A landholding farmer's family is defined as a family consisting of husband, wife, and minor children who own cultivable land in their names as per the land records of the respective State/UT.

chunks.source: PM-Kisan Portal - Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
chunks.content:
Exclusions (Who is NOT Eligible):
The following categories of beneficiaries of higher economic status shall NOT be eligible for benefit under the scheme:
1. Institutional land holders.
2. Farmer families in which one or more of its members belong to the following categories:
   - Former and present holders of constitutional posts.
   - Former and present Ministers/ State Ministers and former/present Members of Lok Sabha/ Rajya Sabha/ State Legislative Assemblies/ State Legislative Councils, former and present Mayors of Municipal Corporations, former and present Chairpersons of District Panchayats.
   - Any serving or retired officers and employees of Central/ State Government Ministries /Offices/Departments and its field units/Central or State PSEs and Attached offices /Autonomous Institutions under Government as well as regular employees of the Local Bodies (Excluding Multi Tasking Staff / Class IV/Group D employees).
   - All superannuated/retired pensioners whose monthly pension is Rs.10,000/- or more (Excluding Multi Tasking Staff / Class IV/Group D employees).
   - All Persons who paid Income Tax in the last assessment year.
   - Professionals like Doctors, Engineers, Lawyers, Chartered Accountants, and Architects registered with Professional bodies and carrying out profession by undertaking practice.

chunks.source: PM-Kisan Portal - Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
chunks.content:
Documents Required:
To register and avail PM-KISAN benefits, farmers need to submit the following documents:
1. Aadhaar Card (mandatory for identity verification and DBT transfer).
2. Land Records / Khasra-Khatauni (proof of landholding in the farmer's name as per state land records).
3. Bank Account Details: Bank passbook or cancelled cheque showing account number linked to Aadhaar.
4. Mobile Number linked to Aadhaar for OTP-based verification.
5. Self-Declaration Form confirming eligibility and that the farmer does not fall under the exclusion categories.
Note: Documents may vary slightly by state. Check with your local Patwari/Lekhpal or Common Service Centre (CSC) for state-specific requirements.

chunks.source: PM-Kisan Portal - Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
chunks.content:
How to Apply (Application Process):
Farmers can register for PM-KISAN through any of the following methods:

Method 1 - Online Registration via Official Portal:
- Visit https://pmkisan.gov.in/
- Click on "Farmers Corner" and then "New Farmer Registration".
- Enter Aadhaar number, state, and captcha, then submit.
- Fill in personal, bank, and land details.
- Submit the form and note the registration reference number.

Method 2 - Common Service Centre (CSC):
- Visit your nearest CSC/Jan Seva Kendra with the required documents.
- The CSC operator will register you on the PM-KISAN portal.

Method 3 - Through Patwari / Agriculture Department:
- Contact your local Patwari, Lekhpal, or District Agriculture Officer.
- They can assist in verifying land records and registering on the portal.

Method 4 - Kisaan e-Mitra Chatbot / PM-KISAN Mobile App:
- Use the official PM-KISAN mobile app (available on Google Play Store) or the Kisaan e-Mitra chatbot on the portal to check status and register.

chunks.source: PM-Kisan Portal - Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
chunks.content:
Status Check:
- Farmers can check beneficiary status at https://pmkisan.gov.in/ under "Farmers Corner" → "Beneficiary Status".
- Enter Aadhaar number, account number, or mobile number to check payment status.

chunks.source: PM-Kisan Portal - Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
chunks.content:
Scheme Duration, Validity & Last Date:
- Last Date / Application Deadline: There is NO last date or closing deadline for PM Kisan Samman Nidhi. It is an ongoing Central Sector scheme of the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare.
- Continuous Registration: Eligible landholding farmers can apply and register on the PM Kisan portal at any time throughout the year.
- Installment Cycle: Installments of ₹2,000 are released every four months (three times a year) directly into registered bank accounts.

chunks.source: National Health Authority - Ayushman Bharat Portal
chunks.content:
Overview:
Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY is the largest health assurance scheme in the world which aims to provide a health cover of Rs. 5 lakhs per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization to over 12 crores poor and vulnerable families (approximately 55 crore beneficiaries) that form the bottom 40% of the Indian population.

chunks.source: National Health Authority - Ayushman Bharat Portal
chunks.content:
Benefits:
- Provides cover of up to Rs. 5,00,000 (Five Lakhs) per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization.
- Provides cashless and paperless access to health care services for the beneficiary at the point of service in any empanelled public or private hospital across India.
- Covers up to 3 days of pre-hospitalization and 15 days post-hospitalization expenses such as diagnostics, medicines, and consultation.
- No restriction on family size, age, or gender.
- All pre-existing medical conditions are covered from day one.
- Coverage Reset: The ₹5 Lakh health insurance cover resets automatically every financial year for eligible family beneficiaries.

chunks.source: National Health Authority - Ayushman Bharat Portal
chunks.content:
Eligibility Criteria (Rural Families):
Under SECC-2011, rural eligibility is determined based on the following deprivation categories (D1 to D7):
- D1: Only one room with kucha walls and kucha roof.
- D2: No adult member between age 16 to 59.
- D3: Female headed households with no adult male member between age 16 to 59.
- D4: Disabled member and no able-bodied adult member.
- D5: Landless households deriving major part of their income from manual casual labour.
- D7: Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) households.
- Automatically included: Destitute, living on alms, manual scavenger households, primitive tribal groups, legally released bonded labour.

chunks.source: National Health Authority - Ayushman Bharat Portal
chunks.content:
Eligibility Criteria (Urban Families):
Under SECC-2011, urban eligibility is defined based on 11 occupational categories:
1. Ragpicker
2. Beggar
3. Domestic worker
4. Street vendor / Cobbler / hawker / Other service provider working on streets
5. Construction worker / Plumber / Mason / Labor / Painter / Welder / Security guard / Coolie and other head-load worker
6. Sweeper / Sanitation worker / Mali
7. Home-based worker / Artisan / Tailor / Handicraft worker
8. Transport worker / Driver / Conductor / Helper to drivers and conductors / Cart puller / Rickshaw puller
9. Shop worker / Assistant / Peon in small establishment / Helper / Delivery assistant / Attendant / Waiter
10. Washerman / Chowkidar
11. Electrician / Mechanic / Assembler / Repair worker

chunks.source: National Health Authority - Ayushman Bharat Portal
chunks.content:
Senior Citizens (Aged 70+):
- All senior citizens aged 70 years and above are eligible for dedicated health insurance cover of ₹5 Lakh per year under the expanded Ayushman Bharat scheme, regardless of socio-economic status.

chunks.source: National Health Authority - Ayushman Bharat Portal
chunks.content:
Documents Required (Part 1/2):
To verify eligibility and generate an Ayushman Card (PM-JAY Golden Card), beneficiaries need:
1. Aadhaar Card: Primary identification document mandatory for biometric / OTP-based e-KYC authentication.
2. Ration Card / Family ID: Proof of family composition and SECC database linkage.
3. Active Mobile Number: Required for receiving OTP during authentication and card download.
4. Government Photo ID (Voter ID / Driving License) in case of auxiliary verification.

chunks.source: National Health Authority - Ayushman Bharat Portal
chunks.content:
Documents Required (Part 2/2):
How to Apply & How to Get Ayushman Card (Application Process):
Eligible beneficiaries can obtain their Ayushman Card through any of the following methods:
1. Online via Beneficiary Portal (https://beneficiary.nha.gov.in/) or Ayushman App:
   - Visit https://beneficiary.nha.gov.in/ or open the official Ayushman App.
   - Login with your mobile number and authenticate via OTP.
   - Select your State, Scheme (PMJAY), and search by Aadhaar Number, Family ID, or PMJAY ID.
   - Complete e-KYC using Aadhaar OTP, Fingerprint, or Face Authentication.
   - Download and print the generated Ayushman Card.
2. Offline at Empanelled Hospital (Ayushman Mitra Help Desk):
   - Visit any empanelled public or private hospital.
   - Meet the Ayushman Mitra at the dedicated Ayushman help desk.
   - Provide your Aadhaar Card and Ration Card to verify eligibility and generate the card on the spot.
3. Offline at Common Service Center (CSC / Jan Seva Kendra):
   - Visit the nearest CSC with Aadhaar card and Ration card.
   - The CSC operator will perform e-KYC and issue the Ayushman Card.

chunks.source: National Health Authority - Ayushman Bharat Portal
chunks.content:
Scheme Duration, Validity & Last Date:
- Last Date / Application Deadline: There is NO last date or closing deadline for Ayushman Bharat (AB-PMJAY). It is a continuous, permanent national health scheme of the Government of India.
- Scheme Validity & Registration: Eligible citizens and senior citizens (aged 70+) can apply for and generate their Ayushman Card at any time throughout the year.
- Benefit Portability: The Ayushman card is portable across all empanelled hospitals in India.

chunks.source: National Government Services Portal - Income Certificate Guidelines
chunks.content:
Overview:
An Income Certificate is an official document issued by the state government authority that certifies the annual income of an individual or a family from all sources (salary, agriculture, business, pension, rental, etc.). It is widely used to claim scholarships, fee concessions, government subsidies, and access to other social welfare schemes.

chunks.source: National Government Services Portal - Income Certificate Guidelines
chunks.content:
Eligibility Criteria:
- The applicant must be a citizen of India.
- The applicant must be a resident of the state/union territory where they are applying.
- The family's combined income from all sources must be declared honestly.

chunks.source: National Government Services Portal - Income Certificate Guidelines
chunks.content:
Documents Required:
1. Proof of Identity: Aadhaar Card, Voter ID Card, PAN Card, or Passport.
2. Proof of Address: Ration Card, Electricity Bill, Water Bill, or Telephone Bill.
3. Proof of Income:
   - For salaried individuals: Form 16, Salary Slip, or Income Tax Return (ITR).
   - For businessmen/professionals: Self-declaration, ITR, or audit reports.
   - For farmers/agriculturists: Land revenue records (e.g., 7/12 extract in some states), Talati/Patwari declaration.
   - For pensioners: Pension payment order (PPO) or bank passbook.
4. Passport-sized photograph.
5. Self-declaration affidavit.

chunks.source: National Government Services Portal - Income Certificate Guidelines
chunks.content:
Application Process:
- Online Method:
  1. Visit the official State e-District portal or Citizen Service Portal (e.g., Digital Gujarat, e-District Delhi, MahaOnline, ServicePlus).
  2. Register or log in to the portal.
  3. Search for "Issue of Income Certificate" under revenue services.
  4. Fill in the application form with personal, address, and income details.
  5. Upload the scanned copies of required documents and a photograph.
  6. Pay the nominal processing fee (varies by state, typically Rs. 10 - Rs. 50).
  7. Submit the application and save the acknowledgment/application number for tracking.
- Offline Method:
  1. Visit the local Tahsildar Office, Mamlatdar Office, Revenue Office, or authorized Citizen Service Centre (CSC) / Jan Seva Kendra.
  2. Obtain and fill out the physical application form.
  3. Attach self-attested photocopies of all required documents.
  4. Submit the form to the officer and obtain a receipt.
  5. The verification is typically done by the local Revenue Inspector or Talati.
  6. The certificate is issued within 10 to 15 days upon successful verification.

chunks.source: National Government Services Portal - Income Certificate Guidelines
chunks.content:
Scheme Validity & Application Deadline:
- Last Date / Application Deadline: There is NO last date or closing deadline for applying for an Income Certificate. Citizen services are available year-round.
- Certificate Validity: Income Certificates are typically valid for 1 financial year (or 3 financial years in specific state jurisdictions like Gujarat/Maharashtra), after which a renewal application is submitted with current income proofs.

chunks.source: National Food Security Portal - Department of Food & Public Distribution
chunks.content:
Overview:
Under the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013, the Government of India provides subsidized and free foodgrains (wheat, rice, coarse grains) to over 80 crore beneficiaries across urban and rural areas through the Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS). Ration cards are official documents issued by State Food and Civil Supplies Departments to enable eligible households to claim their entitlements from designated Fair Price Shops (FPS).

chunks.source: National Food Security Portal - Department of Food & Public Distribution
chunks.content:
Ration Card Categories:
1. Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY): Issued to the poorest of the poor households. Entitled to 35 kg of foodgrains per family per month.
2. Priority Households (PHH): Issued to eligible low-income households as per state criteria. Entitled to 5 kg of foodgrains per person per month.
3. Non-NFSA / General Ration Cards: Issued by state governments for identification and non-subsidized PDS access.

chunks.source: National Food Security Portal - Department of Food & Public Distribution
chunks.content:
Eligibility Criteria:
- Applicant must be an Indian citizen.
- Neither the applicant nor any family member should already possess a active Ration Card in the state.
- Income eligibility limits vary by state and category (AAY households include landless laborers, marginal farmers, widows, disabled heads of house, and destitute persons).

chunks.source: National Food Security Portal - Department of Food & Public Distribution
chunks.content:
Documents Required for Application:
1. Proof of Identity: Aadhaar Card (mandatory for all family members), Voter ID, or PAN Card.
2. Proof of Address: Electricity bill, Water bill, House rent agreement, or Bank passbook.
3. Family Details: Passport-sized photograph of the female head of the family, income certificate, and caste certificate (if applicable).

chunks.source: National Food Security Portal - Department of Food & Public Distribution
chunks.content:
Application Process:
- Online Method:
  1. Visit the state Food and Civil Supplies portal (or access links via https://nfsa.gov.in/).
  2. Register using mobile number and Aadhaar.
  3. Fill out the new Ration Card application form with family member details and address.
  4. Upload scanned copies of required documents and submit.
  5. Save the application reference number to track verification status.
- Offline Method:
  1. Visit the local Ration Office / Food Inspector Office / CSC Center.
  2. Collect and submit the physical application form along with self-attested documents.
  3. Physical inspection/verification is carried out by the local Food Inspector before card generation.

chunks.source: National Food Security Portal - Department of Food & Public Distribution
chunks.content:
Verification Note:
Entitlements, monthly quotas, and state e-Ration Card procedures should be verified directly on the official NFSA portal (https://nfsa.gov.in/) or respective State Food Department portals.

chunks.source: National Food Security Portal - Department of Food & Public Distribution
chunks.content:
Scheme Duration, Validity & Last Date:
- Last Date / Application Deadline: There is NO last date or application deadline for Ration Card / NFSA applications. Applications for new ration cards or member additions are open year-round.
- Beneficiary Entitlement: Free foodgrains (5 kg per person per month for PHH, 35 kg per family per month for AAY) under NFSA are provided on a continuous monthly basis.

chunks.source: PMAY Portal - Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
chunks.ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
chunks.content:
Overview:
Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) is a flagship initiative of the Government of India launched to ensure a pucca house for all eligible urban and rural families. The scheme operates through two verticals: PMAY-Urban (PMAY-U) managed by MoHUA, and PMAY-Gramin (PMAY-G) managed by the Ministry of Rural Development.

chunks.source: PMAY Portal - Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
chunks.ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
chunks.content:
Key Components & Benefits:
1. Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS): Interest subsidy on home loans for EWS, LIG, and MIG categories buying or constructing their first pucca house.
2. Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC): Direct financial assistance (typically Rs. 1.5 Lakh to Rs. 2.5 Lakh depending on state/central share) to eligible families owning land to construct a new house.
3. Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP): Assistance for affordable housing projects built in partnership with public/private sectors.
4. In-Situ Slum Redevelopment (ISSR): Rehabilitation of slum dwellers using land as a resource.

chunks.source: PMAY Portal - Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
chunks.ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
chunks.content:
Eligibility Criteria:
- The beneficiary family must not own a pucca house (an all-weather home) anywhere in India in their name or in the name of any family member.
- Income categories:
  - Economically Weaker Section (EWS): Annual household income up to Rs. 3 Lakh.
  - Low Income Group (LIG): Annual household income between Rs. 3 Lakh and Rs. 6 Lakh.
  - Middle Income Group (MIG-I & MIG-II): Income guidelines specified as per ministry notifications.
- Preference is given to female ownership or co-ownership of the house.

chunks.source: PMAY Portal - Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
chunks.ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
chunks.content:
Documents Required:
1. Proof of Identity & Age: Aadhaar Card (mandatory), Voter ID, PAN Card.
2. Proof of Income: Salary slip, Form 16, Income Certificate from Revenue Authority, or Self-declaration affidavit.
3. Property Documents: Land ownership proof (7/12 extract, registry deed), approved building plan, and site photograph.
4. Bank Account Details: Aadhaar-linked bank account passbook.

chunks.source: PMAY Portal - Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
chunks.ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
chunks.content:
Application Process:
- For PMAY-Urban:
  1. Visit official PMAY-U portal (https://pmaymis.gov.in/) or visit nearest Common Service Center (CSC).
  2. Navigate to 'Citizen Assessment' and select relevant category (e.g. Beneficiary Led Construction).
  3. Enter Aadhaar number and fill out personal, income, and bank details.
  4. Submit application and download assessment form for tracking.
- For PMAY-Gramin:
  1. Beneficiary selection is based on Housing Deprivation parameters in SECC 2011 data verified by Gram Sabha.

chunks.source: PMAY Portal - Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
chunks.ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
chunks.content:
Verification Note:
Specific subsidy amounts, active CLSS guidelines, and beneficiary lists should be verified on the official portals (https://pmaymis.gov.in/ and https://pmayg.nic.in/).

chunks.source: PMAY Portal - Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
chunks.ministry: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
chunks.content:
Scheme Duration, Validity & Last Date:
- Last Date / Extension: The Cabinet has extended Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY Urban 2.0 & PMAY Gramin) to cover 3 crore additional houses through 2028-2029.
- Application Deadline: Applications remain open continuously on the official PMAY portal and through local Gram Panchayats / CSC centers.

chunks.source: e-Shram Portal - Ministry of Labour & Employment
chunks.content:
Overview:
e-Shram is a comprehensive national database created by the Ministry of Labour & Employment to register and deliver social security benefits to unorganized workers across India. Registered workers are issued an e-Shram Card containing a unique 12-digit Universal Account Number (UAN).

chunks.source: e-Shram Portal - Ministry of Labour & Employment
chunks.content:
Eligible Worker Categories:
Unorganized workers aged between 16 and 59 years, including:
- Construction workers, plumbers, masons, painters, electricians.
- Small and marginal farmers, agricultural laborers, sharecroppers.
- Street vendors, hawkers, rickshaw pullers, coolies, head-load workers.
- Domestic workers, maids, tailors, weavers, handicraft artisans.
- Gig and platform workers, delivery agents, drivers.

chunks.source: e-Shram Portal - Ministry of Labour & Employment
chunks.content:
Key Benefits:
1. Universal Account Number (UAN): A portable 12-digit identification valid across all states in India.
2. Accidental Insurance Cover: Rs. 2 Lakh cover in case of accidental death or permanent disability, and Rs. 1 Lakh for partial disability under Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY).
3. Social Security Scheme Integration: Seamless integration for government welfare schemes (such as PMSYM pension scheme, ration benefits, emergency relief funds during disasters).

chunks.source: e-Shram Portal - Ministry of Labour & Employment
chunks.content:
Eligibility Exclusions:
- Workers who are members of EPFO (Employees' Provident Fund) or ESIC (Employees' State Insurance).
- Individuals who pay Income Tax in the last assessment year.
- Persons under 16 years or above 59 years of age.

chunks.source: e-Shram Portal - Ministry of Labour & Employment
chunks.content:
Documents Required:
1. Aadhaar Card (with active mobile number linked for OTP verification).
2. Aadhaar-linked Active Bank Account details (Bank Name, Account Number, IFSC Code).
3. Occupation details and educational qualification proof (optional).

chunks.source: e-Shram Portal - Ministry of Labour & Employment
chunks.content:
Self-Registration Process:
1. Visit the official e-Shram portal (https://eshram.gov.in/) and click 'Register on e-Shram'.
2. Enter Aadhaar-linked mobile number and captcha code, then enter OTP received.
3. Verify Aadhaar details using OTP/Biometric.
4. Fill in personal details, address, occupation, educational qualification, and bank details.
5. Preview and submit the form. Download and print the e-Shram Card instantly.

chunks.source: e-Shram Portal - Ministry of Labour & Employment
chunks.content:
Verification Note:
Worker registration is free of cost. Check current registration status and update profile details at the official portal (https://eshram.gov.in/).

chunks.source: e-Shram Portal - Ministry of Labour & Employment
chunks.content:
Scheme Duration, Validity & Last Date:
- Last Date / Application Deadline: There is NO last date or closing deadline for e-Shram registration. Registration remains open 24/7 year-round.
- Card Validity: The e-Shram UWIN card is valid for a lifetime. Workers can update their occupation, address, or bank details at any time.

chunks.source: Passport Seva - Ministry of External Affairs
chunks.content:
Overview:
Passport Seva Project, administered by the Consular, Passport & Visa (CPV) Division of the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), provides citizen-centric passport services across India through Passport Seva Kendras (PSK), Post Office Passport Seva Kendras (POPSK), and official online portals.

chunks.source: Passport Seva - Ministry of External Affairs
chunks.content:
Types of Passport Applications:
1. Fresh Passport: Applied for the first time.
2. Re-issue of Passport: Applied when existing passport has expired, pages are exhausted, or details (address/name) are updated.
3. Tatkaal Passport: Urgent processing category for fast-track passport issuance.

chunks.source: Passport Seva - Ministry of External Affairs
chunks.content:
Eligibility Criteria:
- Applicant must be an Indian citizen.
- Applicants of any age (including minors and senior citizens) can apply with valid proof.

chunks.source: Passport Seva - Ministry of External Affairs
chunks.content:
Documents Required:
1. Proof of Date of Birth: Birth Certificate, Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, School Leaving Certificate, or Driving License.
2. Proof of Present Address: Aadhaar Card, Bank Passbook (with photo), Electricity Bill, Water Bill, Rent Agreement, or Voter ID.
3. Non-ECR Proof (for ECNR status): Class 10th pass certificate or higher educational qualification certificate, income tax assessment order, or proof of age above 50.
4. For Re-issue: Original existing passport and self-attested photocopies of first two and last two pages.

chunks.source: Passport Seva - Ministry of External Affairs
chunks.content:
Application Process:
1. Register on official portal (https://www.passportindia.gov.in/) and log in to user account.
2. Click 'Apply for Fresh Passport / Re-issue of Passport'.
3. Fill out online application form (or download e-form, fill offline, and upload).
4. Click 'Pay and Schedule Appointment' to select nearest Passport Seva Kendra (PSK/POPSK) and choose an available date/time slot.
5. Pay application fee online (Credit/Debit Card, Net Banking, or SBI Challan).
6. Print application receipt containing Application Reference Number (ARN).
7. Visit designated PSK/POPSK on appointment date with original documents for biometric capture and document verification.
8. Police Verification is initiated locally before/after passport dispatch depending on application category.

chunks.source: Passport Seva - Ministry of External Affairs
chunks.content:
Verification Note:
Fee structures, Tatkaal rules, and appointment availability should be verified directly on the official portal (https://www.passportindia.gov.in/).

chunks.source: Passport Seva - Ministry of External Affairs
chunks.content:
Scheme Duration, Validity & Last Date:
- Last Date / Application Deadline: There is NO last date or application deadline for Passport Seva services. Applications for new passports, renewals, and Tatkaal passports are open 365 days a year.
- Passport Validity: Standard adult passports are valid for 10 years (5 years for minors), after which a renewal application is submitted.

chunks.source: Mudra Portal - Ministry of Finance
chunks.content:
Overview:
Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) is a scheme initiated by the Government of India to provide collateral-free business loans up to Rs. 10 Lakh to non-corporate, non-farm small and micro enterprises (MSMEs). Loans are disbursed through Commercial Banks, RRBs, Small Finance Banks, MFIs, and NBFCs.

chunks.source: Mudra Portal - Ministry of Finance
chunks.content:
Mudra Loan Categories:
1. Shishu: Loans up to Rs. 50,000/- (aimed at startups and new small entrepreneurs).
2. Kishor: Loans above Rs. 50,000/- and up to Rs. 5 Lakh (for existing micro enterprises expanding operations).
3. Tarun: Loans above Rs. 5 Lakh and up to Rs. 10 Lakh (for established business units upgrading machinery or infrastructure).

chunks.source: Mudra Portal - Ministry of Finance
chunks.content:
Eligibility Criteria:
- Any Indian citizen who has a viable business plan for a non-farm sector income-generating activity (manufacturing, trading, services, agriculture-allied activities like poultry/dairy).
- The applicant must not be a defaulter to any bank or financial institution.

chunks.source: Mudra Portal - Ministry of Finance
chunks.content:
Key Benefits:
- Collateral-Free Credit: No collateral security required for loans up to Rs. 10 Lakh under Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units (CGFMU).
- Flexible Repayment: Repayment tenure typically ranges between 3 and 5 years.
- Mudra Card: Issued as a RuPay debit card for convenient working capital drawdown.

chunks.source: Mudra Portal - Ministry of Finance
chunks.content:
Documents Required:
1. Proof of Identity: Voter ID, Aadhaar Card, Driving License, or PAN Card.
2. Proof of Residence: Utility bill, Bank passbook, or Aadhaar Card.
3. Business Proof: Business registration certificate, GST registration, trade license, or partnership deed.
4. Financial Proof: Bank account statements for past 6 months, quotation for machinery/equipment, and project report with projected cash flows.
5. Passport-sized photographs of applicant/partners.

chunks.source: Mudra Portal - Ministry of Finance
chunks.content:
Application Process:
1. Prepare business plan, quotation for items to purchase, and financial/KYC documents.
2. Approach any participating Public/Private Sector Bank, Regional Rural Bank, or NBFC branch.
3. Alternatively, apply online via JanSamarth portal (https://www.jansamarth.in/) under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana.
4. Fill application form, attach documents, and submit for credit assessment.

chunks.source: Mudra Portal - Ministry of Finance
chunks.content:
Verification Note:
Interest rates vary by lender bank based on RBI/Mudra guidelines. Check details at https://www.mudra.org.in/ or official bank branches.

chunks.source: Mudra Portal - Ministry of Finance
chunks.content:
Scheme Duration, Validity & Last Date:
- Last Date / Application Deadline: There is NO last date or closing deadline for Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY). It is an ongoing central micro-finance scheme.
- Application Availability: Micro-entrepreneurs and small business owners can apply for Mudra loans year-round through commercial banks, RRBs, MFIs, and JanSamarth portal.

chunks.source: National Scholarship Portal - Ministry of Electronics & IT
chunks.content:
Overview:
National Scholarship Portal (NSP) is a one-stop digital platform introduced by the Government of India to streamline scholarship applications, verification, and Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) disbursement for students across Central Government Ministries, State Education Departments, and AICTE/UGC schemes.

chunks.source: National Scholarship Portal - Ministry of Electronics & IT
chunks.content:
Major Scholarship Categories:
1. Central Sector Schemes: Offered by Ministry of Social Justice, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Ministry of Minority Affairs, Department of Higher Education, and Department of School Education.
2. UGC / AICTE Schemes: Technical and professional education scholarships for single girl child, PG scholarship, and Pragati/Saksham schemes.
3. State Schemes: State-specific pre-matric and post-matric financial assistance for SC, ST, OBC, EBC, and PwD students.

chunks.source: National Scholarship Portal - Ministry of Electronics & IT
chunks.content:
Eligibility Criteria:
- Applicant must be an Indian citizen enrolled in a recognized school, college, university, or institute in India.
- Minimum academic marks (e.g. 50% or 60% in previous qualifying exam) as specified by individual scheme guidelines.
- Annual family income limits vary by scheme (typically up to Rs. 1 Lakh for Pre-Matric, Rs. 2.5 Lakh for Post-Matric, or up to Rs. 8 Lakh for Top Class Education).

chunks.source: National Scholarship Portal - Ministry of Electronics & IT
chunks.content:
Documents Required for Application:
1. Aadhaar Card / Aadhaar Enrolment Slip (mandatory for DBT payment).
2. Student Bank Passbook (account linked with Aadhaar and active for DBT).
3. Educational Certificates: Marksheets of previous passed examination.
4. Income Certificate: Issued by designated State Revenue Authority (Tahsildar/Mamlatdar).
5. Caste / Category Certificate (SC/ST/OBC/Minority) where applicable.
6. Bonafide Student Certificate issued by the current Institute/School.
7. Fee receipt of current academic year.

chunks.source: National Scholarship Portal - Ministry of Electronics & IT
chunks.content:
Application Process:
1. Visit official NSP portal (https://scholarships.gov.in/).
2. Click 'New Registration' and complete One Time Registration (OTR) using Aadhaar-linked mobile.
3. Obtain OTR ID and password via SMS.
4. Log in to student portal and select appropriate scholarship scheme based on eligibility.
5. Fill personal, academic, fee, and bank details.
6. Upload scanned copies of required documents and submit application.
7. Application undergoes 2-tier online verification: first by Institute Nodal Officer (INO), followed by District/State Nodal Officer (DNO/SNO).
8. Verified funds are transferred directly into student bank accounts via Aadhaar Payment Bridge (APB).

chunks.source: National Scholarship Portal - Ministry of Electronics & IT
chunks.content:
Verification Note:
Scheme application open dates, income ceilings, and verification deadlines should be verified on the official NSP portal (https://scholarships.gov.in/).

chunks.source: National Scholarship Portal - Ministry of Electronics & IT
chunks.content:
Scheme Duration, Validity & Last Date:
- Academic Application Window: National Scholarship Portal (NSP) applications open annually for each academic year (typically between July/August and December/January).
- Application Deadline: Students must submit online applications before the state/ministry-specific deadline published annually on https://scholarships.gov.in/ (usually extended till late December or January). Existing beneficiaries submit annual renewal applications.
